newsitem.title: PERU: Peru launches inquiry into phone spying scandal.
newsitem.headline: Peru launches inquiry into phone spying scandal.

text.p: The Peruvian government on Tuesday authorised a special public prosecutor to investigate allegations of telephone espionage by secret service agents.
A decree in the official daily El Peruano promised a "meticulous investigation" to track down those responsible and guarantee people's privacy.
The measure, signed by Interior Minister Gen. Jose Villanueva Ruesta, was widely interpreted as an attempt to counter the scandal's effect on President Alberto Fujimori's popularity.
The allegations surfaced in July when a local television station aired a report accusing the secret services of tapping the telephones of 197 politicians, journalists, artists and businessmen.

Former United Nations chief Javier Perez de Cuellar, who leads Peru's opposition, aggravated the scandal on Tuesday by lodging formal legal complaint that the government tapped his telephones during the 1995 presidential campaign. He lost the election to Fujimori.

The government has repeatedly denied involvement in phone-tapping, saying amateurs might have used simple electronic devices to listen in on conversations. But polls show a majority of Peruvians believe Fujimori's government is responsible.
The scandal has contributed to Fujimori's slide in approval ratings in recent months to a record low of 19 percent in mid-July.

But a new poll on Tuesday showed the president's popularity back up to 33 percent, thanks to tax breaks and salary increases he announced during last week's State of the Nation address. Imasen's poll of 400 people also showed that 92.5 percent favoured an investigation into the accusations of telephone espionage.
The pollster did not give a margin of error.
